section.heading: Relationship with Part 7B of the Interactive Gambling Act 2001

content.p: This Part does not authorise a disclosure of information that is prohibited by Part 7B of the Interactive Gambling 2001.
Omit:

• This Part sets up a mechanism that allows individuals to exclude themselves from being provided with licensed interactive wagering services.
• The ACMA must arrange for a body corporate to keep a register to be known as the National Self-exclusion Register. The body corporate is to be known as the Register operator.
• An individual may apply to the Register operator for the individual to be registered in the National Self-exclusion Register.
• A licensed interactive wagering service provider must not:
provide a licensed interactive wagering service to a registered individual; or
send, or cause to be sent, a regulated electronic message to an electronic address of a registered individual; or
make, or cause to be made, a regulated telemarketing call to a registered individual; or
send, or cause to be sent, regulated direct marketing material to a registered individual; or
disclose information about a registered individual for marketing purposes; or
open a licensed interactive wagering service account for a registered individual.
• The Register operator must, if requested to do so by a licensed interactive wagering service provider, inform the provider whether an individual is a registered individual.

section.heading: When an outstanding or pending bet is resolved

content.p: For the purposes of this Part:
(a) if an outstanding or pending bet turns out to be a winning bet—the bet is resolved when the bet is settled; and
(b) if an outstanding or pending bet turns out to be a losing bet—the bet is resolved when it becomes clear that the bet is a losing bet; and
(c) if the bettor becomes entitled to a refund of the bet—the bet is resolved when it becomes clear that the bettor has become entitled to a refund of the bet.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c), it is immaterial whether a refund is or will be made by way of a credit to a licensed interactive wagering service account.
(1) For the purposes of this Part, an electronic message is a message sent:
using:
an internet carriage service; or
any other listed carriage service; and
to an electronic address in connection with:
an email account; or
an instant messaging account; or
a telephone account; or
a similar account.
Note: Email addresses and telephone numbers are examples of electronic addresses.
For the purposes of subsection (1), it is immaterial whether the electronic address exists.
For the purposes of subsection (1), it is immaterial whether the message reaches its intended destination.
Subsection (1) has effect subject to subsection (5).
Excluded messages—voice calls
(5) If a message is sent by way of a voice call, the message is not an electronic message for the purposes of this Part.
(1) For the purposes of this Part, a regulated electronic message is an electronic message, where, having regard to:
the content of the message; and
the way in which the message is presented; and
the content that can be located using the links, telephone numbers or contact information (if any) set out in the message;
it would be concluded that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the message is:
to offer to provide licensed interactive wagering services; or
to advertise or promote licensed interactive wagering services; or
to advertise or promote a provider, or prospective provider, of licensed interactive wagering services.
Paragraphs (1)(d), (e) and (f) are to be read independently of each other.
(1) For the purposes of this Part, a regulated telemarketing call is a voice call, where, having regard to:
the content of the call; and
the presentational aspects of the call; and
the content that can be obtained using the numbers, URLs or contact information (if any) mentioned in the call; and
if:
the call is made from a telephone number; and
that number is disclosed to the recipient (whether by calling line identification or otherwise);
the content (if any) that can be obtained by calling that number;
it would be concluded that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the call is:
to offer to provide licensed interactive wagering services; or
to advertise or promote licensed interactive wagering services; or
to advertise or promote a provider, or prospective provider, of licensed interactive wagering services.
Paragraphs (1)(e), (f) and (g) are to be read independently of each other.
(1) For the purposes of this Part, regulated direct marketing material means physical material, where, having regard to:
the content of the material; and
the way in which the material is presented; and
the content that can be located using the URLs, telephone numbers or contact information (if any) set out in the material;
it would be concluded that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the material is:
to offer to provide licensed interactive wagering services; or
to advertise or promote licensed interactive wagering services; or
to advertise or promote a provider, or prospective provider, of licensed interactive wagering services.
Paragraphs (1)(d), (e) and (f) are to be read independently of each other.
(1) The ACMA must arrange for a body corporate (the Register operator) to keep, on behalf of the ACMA, a register to be known as the National Self-exclusion Register.
The register may also be known by a name specified in the Register rules.
The register is to be kept in electronic form.
The register is not a legislative instrument.
Payments to the Register operator
An arrangement under subsection (1) may provide for the ACMA, on behalf of the Commonwealth, to make payments to the Register operator.
Register operator must not provide a gambling service or undertake gambling-related lobbying etc.
The ACMA must not make an arrangement under subsection (1) with a body corporate that:
provides a gambling service; or
is a member of the same related company group as a body corporate that provides a gambling service; or
holds an ownership interest in a body corporate that provides a gambling service; or
undertakes gambling-related lobbying; or
is a member of the same related company group as a body corporate that undertakes gambling-related lobbying; or
holds an ownership interest in a body corporate that undertakes gambling-related lobbying.
The ACMA must ensure that an arrangement under subsection (1) is subject to a condition that the Register operator must not:
provide a gambling service; or
be a member of the same related company group as a body corporate that provides a gambling service; or
hold an ownership interest in a body corporate that provides a gambling service; or
undertake gambling-related lobbying; or
be a member of the same related company group as a body corporate that undertakes gambling-related lobbying; or
hold an ownership interest in a body corporate that undertakes gambling-related lobbying.

division.heading: Registration in the National Self-exclusion Register

content.p: An individual may apply to the Register operator for the individual to be registered in the National Self-exclusion Register.
An application under subsection (1) must:
state that the applicant wants to be registered for a specified number of months; or
state that the applicant wants to be registered for a specified number of years; or
state that the applicant wants to be registered for life.
The number of months specified under paragraph (2)(a):
must be a whole number; and
must not be less than 3.
The number of years specified under paragraph (2)(b) must be a whole number.
An application under subsection (1) must be made in a manner prescribed by the Register rules.
An application under subsection (1) must:
include a statement to the effect that the applicant is ordinarily resident in Australia; and
include such information relating to the applicant as is prescribed by the Register rules.
Nominated support person
An application under subsection (1) may:
nominate:
another individual to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 2 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 3 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 4 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 5 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; and
include a statement to the effect that the applicant has obtained the consent of the other individual, or each of the other individuals, to be a nominated support person of the applicant; and
include such information relating to the other individual, or each of the other individuals, as is prescribed by the Register rules.
Reactivation of a previous registration
If:
an application is made under subsection (1); and
the applicant ceased to be a registered individual on one or more occasions during the 7-year period ending when the application was made; and
the applicant gave an archived records consent that is applicable to the most recent cessation of registration; and
the application includes a statement to the effect that the applicant wants to reactivate the applicant’s previous registration;
then:

the Register operator may use any or all of the information and statements included in the applicant’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register (as it stood immediately before that most recent cessation of registration) to prefill any or all of the fields in the application; and
the applicant may delete or modify any or all of the prefilled information or statements before finalising the application.
Proclaimed start day
An individual is not entitled to make an application under subsection (1) before the proclaimed start day.

If an individual makes an application under section 61JA to be registered in the National Self-exclusion Register, the Register operator must attempt to carry out the applicable identification procedure in respect of the applicant.
Subsection (1) does not apply if a recognised third-party identification procedure has been carried out in respect of the applicant.
Subsection (1) does not apply if:
the applicant ceased to be a registered individual on one or more occasions during the 7-year period ending when the application was made; and
the applicant gave an archived records consent that is applicable to the most recent cessation of registration; and
the application includes a statement to the effect that the applicant wants to reactivate the applicant’s previous registration.
If:
(a) an individual (the relevant individual) makes an application under section 61JA to be registered in the National Self-exclusion Register; and
either:
the Register operator has carried out the applicable identification procedure in respect of the relevant individual; or
as a result of subsection 61JB(2) or (3), the Register operator is not required to attempt to carry out the applicable identification procedure in respect of the relevant individual;
the Register operator must:
register the relevant individual by making an entry for the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register; and
do so within the period ascertained in accordance with the Register rules.
The entry must include:
the relevant individual’s name; and
if the application nominated:
another individual to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 2 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 3 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 4 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant; or
each of 5 other individuals to be a nominated support person of the applicant;
for each nominated individual:
a statement to the effect that the individual is a nominated support person of the relevant individual; and
such other information relating to the individual as is prescribed by the Register rules.
If the entry includes a statement to the effect that another individual is a nominated support person of the relevant individual, the Register operator must:
notify the other individual:
that the Register operator has registered the relevant individual; and
that the other individual is a nominated support person of the relevant individual; and
of such other information (if any) as is prescribed by the Register rules; and
do so as soon as practicable after registering the relevant individual.
Offence—bribery
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a licensed interactive wagering service provider; and
the person:
provides a benefit to an individual; or
causes a benefit to be provided to an individual; or
offers to provide, or promises to provide, a benefit to an individual; or
causes an offer of the provision of a benefit, or a promise of the provision of a benefit, to be made to an individual; and
the person does so with the intention of influencing the individual:
not to become a registered individual; or
to cease to be a registered individual.
Penalty: 120 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision—bribery
A licensed interactive wagering service provider must not:
provide a benefit to an individual; or
cause a benefit to be provided to an individual; or
offer to provide, or promise to provide, a benefit to an individual; or
cause an offer of the provision of a benefit, or a promise of the provision of a benefit, to be made to an individual;
with the intention of influencing the individual:
not to become a registered individual; or
to cease to be a registered individual.
Civil penalty: 180 penalty units.
Offence—influence
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a licensed interactive wagering service provider; and
the person does an act or thing; and
the person does the act or thing with the intention of influencing an individual:
not to become a registered individual; or
to cease to be a registered individual.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision—influence
A licensed interactive wagering service provider must not do an act or thing with the intention of influencing an individual:
not to become a registered individual; or
to cease to be a registered individual.
Civil penalty: 90 penalty units.
Offence—extended geographical jurisdiction
(5) Section 15.4 of the Criminal Code (extended geographical jurisdiction—category D) applies to an offence against subsection (1) or (3).

If an individual’s entry is removed from the National Self-exclusion Register, this Act does not prevent the Register operator from subsequently re-registering the individual under subsection 61JC(1).
Registration for a number of months
If:
in response to an application under section 61JA, the Register operator registers an individual by making an entry for the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register; and
the application stated that the individual wants to be registered for a specified number of months;
the registration remains in force for that number of months.
Subsection (1) has effect subject to sections 61JG, 61JK, 61JM and 61JN.
Registration for a number of years
If:
in response to an application under section 61JA, the Register operator registers an individual by making an entry for the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register; and
the application stated that the individual wants to be registered for a specified number of years;
the registration remains in force for that number of years.
Subsection (3) has effect subject to sections 61JG, 61JK, 61JM and 61JN.
Registration for life
If:
in response to an application under section 61JA, the Register operator registers an individual by making an entry for the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register; and
the application stated that the individual wants to be registered for life;
the registration remains in force for the life of the individual.
Subsection (5) has effect subject to sections 61JK, 61JM and 61JN.
Nominated support person to be notified of duration of registration
If:
the Register operator registers an individual by making an entry for the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register; and
the individual has a nominated support person;
the Register operator must:
notify the nominated support person of the duration of the individual’s registration; and
do so as soon as practicable after registering the individual.
A registered individual may:
apply to the Register operator to extend the duration of the individual’s registration by a specified number of months; or
apply to the Register operator to extend the duration of the individual’s registration by a specified number of years; or
apply to the Register operator to extend the duration of the individual’s registration to the end of the individual’s life.
A number of months specified under paragraph (1)(a) must be a whole number.
A number of years specified under paragraph (1)(b) must be a whole number.
An application under subsection (1) must:
include such information (if any) as is prescribed by the Register rules; and
be made in a manner prescribed by the Register rules.

If a registered individual makes an application under subsection (1) to extend the duration of the individual’s registration by a specified number of months, the Register operator must extend the duration of the individual’s registration by that number of months.

If a registered individual makes an application under subsection (1) to extend the duration of the individual’s registration by a specified number of years, the Register operator must extend the duration of the individual’s registration by that number of years.

If a registered individual makes an application under subsection (1) to extend the duration of the individual’s registration to the end of the individual’s life, the Register operator must extend the duration of the individual’s registration to the end of the individual’s life.
If:
the Register operator extends the duration of a registered individual’s registration; and
the individual has a nominated support person;
the Register operator must:
notify the nominated support person of:
the extension; and
if the extension is not to the end of the individual’s life—the time when the individual’s registration will expire as a result of the extension; and
do so as soon as practicable after making the extension.
If the registration of a registered individual expires, the Register operator must remove the individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register.
If the registration of a registered individual will expire at a known time, the Register operator must:
notify the individual that the individual’s registration will expire at that time; and
do so at least 14 days before that time.
If:
the registration of a registered individual will expire at a known time; and
the individual has a nominated support person;
the Register operator must:
notify the nominated support person that the individual’s registration will expire at that time; and
do so at least 14 days before that time.

section.heading: Variation of the National Self-exclusion Register—nominated support person

content.p: New nominated support person
The Register rules may authorise the Register operator to vary a registered individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register by including:
a statement to the effect that another individual is a nominated support person of the registered individual; and
such information relating to the other individual as is prescribed by the Register rules.

(2) If, as the result of a variation under Register rules made for the purposes of subsection (1), an individual (the relevant individual) becomes a nominated support person of a registered individual, the Register operator must:
notify the relevant individual that the relevant individual has become a nominated support person of the registered individual; and
do so as soon as practicable after the relevant individual becomes a nominated support person of the registered individual.
Ceasing to be a nominated support person
The Register rules may authorise the Register operator to vary a registered individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register by deleting:
a statement relating to a nominated support person of the registered individual; and
any information relating to the nominated support person.

(4) If, as the result of a variation under Register rules made for the purposes of subsection (3), an individual (the former nominated support person) ceases to be a nominated support person of a registered individual, the Register operator must:
notify the former nominated support person of the cessation; and
do so as soon as practicable after the cessation.
Death of nominated support person
The Register rules may provide that, if:
a registered individual has a nominated support person; and
the Register operator becomes aware that the nominated support person has died;
the Register operator must vary the registered individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register by deleting:
the statement relating to the nominated support person; and
any information relating to the nominated support person.
Other matters

The Register operator must not vary a registered individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register if doing so would result in the registered individual having more than 5 nominated support persons.
This section does not, by implication, limit section 61JJ.

section.heading: Variation of the National Self-exclusion Register—other matters

content.p: The Register rules may authorise the Register operator to vary entries in the National Self-exclusion Register.
A registered individual may apply to the Register operator to remove the individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register.

However, a registered individual is not entitled to make an application under subsection (1) during the 3-month period beginning at the time when the individual’s registration came into force, unless the individual was previously registered before that time.
An application under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
include such information (if any) as is prescribed by the Register rules.
An application made by a registered individual under subsection (1) must be accompanied by a statutory declaration:
that is made by the registered individual; and
that:

is to the effect that, during the 3-month period ending when the application was made, the registered individual obtained counselling or advice from a qualified counsellor about the registered individual’s decision to make the application; or

is to the effect that, during the 3-month period ending when the application was made, the registered individual obtained counselling or advice from a qualified psychologist about the registered individual’s decision to make the application; or

is to the effect that, during the 3-month period ending when the application was made, the registered individual obtained counselling or advice from a general practitioner about the registered individual’s decision to make the application; or

is to the effect that, during the 3-month period ending when the application was made, the registered individual obtained counselling or advice from a listed support service about the registered individual’s decision to make the application.
If:
a registered individual makes an application under subsection (1) to remove the individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register; and
the registered individual has a nominated support person;
the Register operator must:
inform the nominated support person:
that the application has been made; and
that the application can be withdrawn by the registered individual before the end of the seventh day after the day the application was made; and

that, if the application is not withdrawn, the registered individual’s entry will be removed from the National Self-exclusion Register at the start of the eighth day after the day the application was made; and
if the application is not withdrawn by the registered individual before the end of the seventh day after the day the application was made:
remove the registered individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register at the start of the eighth day after the day the application was made; and
notify the nominated support person of the removal; and
if the application is withdrawn by the registered individual before the end of the seventh day after the day the application was made—notify the nominated support person of the withdrawal.
If:
a registered individual makes an application under subsection (1) to remove the individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register; and
the registered individual does not have a nominated support person; and
the application is not withdrawn by the registered individual before the end of the seventh day after the day the application was made;
the Register operator must remove the registered individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register at the start of the eighth day after the day the application was made.
An individual may make a statement to the Register operator:

to the effect that, in the event that the individual ceases to be a registered individual, the individual consents to the Register operator archiving a copy of the individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register (as it stood immediately before the cessation) for 7 years after the cessation; and
acknowledging that the archived copy can be used by the Register operator to facilitate a subsequent re-registration of the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register.
(2) A consent under subsection (1) is to be known as an archived records consent.
A statement under subsection (1) may be included in an application made under this Part or the Register rules.

If an individual has given an archived records consent, the relevant archived copy of the individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register may only be used by the Register operator to facilitate a subsequent re-registration of the individual in the National Self-exclusion Register.
The Register operator must remove a registered individual’s entry from the National Self-exclusion Register if the Register operator is aware that:
the individual is not ordinarily resident in Australia; or
the individual has died.

section.heading: Correction of the National Self-exclusion Register

content.p: The Register operator may correct entries in the National Self-exclusion Register.
The ACMA may give written directions to the Register operator relating to the exercise of its powers under subsection (1).
The Register operator must comply with a direction under subsection (2).

content.p: The Register rules may make further provision in relation to the National Self-exclusion Register.

section.heading: Licensed interactive wagering service providers must promote the National Self-exclusion Register etc.

content.p: The Register rules may require licensed interactive wagering service providers to take specified action for the purposes of promoting the National Self-exclusion Register to their customers.

The Register rules may require licensed interactive wagering service providers to take specified action directed towards ensuring that their customers are aware of, and can readily access, the following:
the website of the National Self-exclusion Register;
if there is an app for the National Self-exclusion Register—that app.
Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a licensed interactive wagering service provider; and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct contravenes Register rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: 120 penalty units.
A person who contravenes subsection (3) commits a separate offence in respect of each day (including a day of conviction for the offence or any later day) during which the contravention continues.
Civil penalty provision
A licensed interactive wagering service provider must not contravene Register rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty: 180 penalty units.

A person who contravenes subsection (5) commits a separate contravention of that provision in respect of each day during which the contravention occurs (including the day the relevant civil penalty order is made or any later day).
Exception
Subsections (3) and (5) do not apply if the contravention occurred in circumstances prescribed by the Register rules.
Note 1: In a prosecution for an offence against subsection (3), a defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).

Note 2: In proceedings for a civil penalty order for a contravention of subsection (5), a defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see section 96 of the Regulatory Powers Act).

section.heading: Closure of a licensed interactive wagering service account held by a registered individual—no outstanding or pending bets

content.p: Offence
If:
an individual becomes a registered individual; and
immediately before becoming a registered individual:
the individual had a licensed interactive wagering service account with a licensed interactive wagering service provider; and
the individual did not have any outstanding or pending bets that are attributable to the provision of a licensed interactive wagering service by the provider;
then:

if, immediately before becoming a registered individual, the individual did not owe any debts to the provider that could lawfully be recovered by way of deduction from the account—the provider must, as soon as practicable after the individual becomes a registered individual:
close the account; and
if the account has a credit balance—pay the individual an amount equal to the credit balance; and

if, immediately before becoming a registered individual, the individual owed one or more debts to the provider that could lawfully be recovered by way of deduction from the account—the provider must, as soon as practicable after the individual becomes a registered individual:
close the account; and

if the account would have a credit balance if the total amount of those debts were deducted from the account—pay the individual an amount equal to the difference between the balance of the account and the total amount of those debts; and

if the individual ceases to be a registered individual before the closure of the account—the provider must ensure that the account is not used in relation to the provision, or prospective provision, of one or more licensed interactive wagering services to the individual after the cessation; and
if the account has been closed—the provider must not reopen, reactivate or reinstate the account.

Paragraph (1)(e) does not prevent the licensed interactive wagering service provider from opening a new licensed interactive wagering service account for the individual if the individual ceases to be a registered individual.

For the purposes of this Part, protected information means:
information about whether an individual is or was a registered individual; or
information about whether an individual is or was a nominated support person of a registered individual; or
any other information that is or was included in an entry in the National Self-exclusion Register; or
information about, or included in, an application made by an individual under Division 3 or the Register rules.
Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person discloses protected information; and
the person is or was:
a licensed interactive wagering service provider; or
an employee of a licensed interactive wagering service provider; or
a contracted service provider of a licensed interactive wagering service provider; or
an employee of a contracted service provider of a licensed interactive wagering service provider; or
the Register operator; or
an employee of the Register operator; or
a contracted service provider of the Register operator; or
an employee of a contracted service provider of the Register operator; or
an ACMA official; or
the Secretary of a Department; or
an APS employee in a Department; and
the information has come to the person’s knowledge, or into the person’s possession:
if the person is or was a licensed interactive wagering service provider—in connection with the person’s capacity as such a provider; or
if the person is or was an employee of a licensed interactive wagering service provider—because the person is or was employed by the provider in connection with its business as such a provider; or
if the person is or was a contracted service provider of a licensed interactive wagering service provider—in connection with the person’s business as such a contracted service provider; or

if the person is or was an employee of a contracted service provider of a licensed interactive wagering service provider—because the person is or was employed by the contracted service provider in connection with its business as such a contracted service provider; or
if the person is or was the Register operator—in connection with the person’s capacity as the Register operator; or
if the person is or was an employee of the Register operator—because the person is or was employed by the Register operator in connection with its business as the Register operator; or
if the person is or was a contracted service provider of the Register operator—in connection with the person’s business as such a contracted service provider; or

if the person is or was an employee of a contracted service provider of the Register operator—because the person is or was employed by the contracted service provider in connection with its business as such a contracted service provider; or
if the person is or was an ACMA official—in connection with the person’s capacity as an ACMA official; or
if the person is or was the Secretary of a Department—in connection with the person’s capacity as the Secretary of that Department; or
if the person is or was an APS employee in a Department—in connection with the person’s capacity as an APS employee in that Department.

Note 2: In proceedings for a civil penalty order for a contravention of subsection (2), a defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see section 96 of the Regulatory Powers Act).
Authorised disclosure—general
A person covered by paragraph (1)(b) or (2)(a) may disclose protected information:
in connection with the administration or execution of this Part; or
for the purposes of ensuring that a licensed interactive wagering service provider complies with this Part; or
for the purposes of:
any legal proceedings arising out of or otherwise related to this Part; or
any report of any such proceedings; or

in connection with the performance of functions, or the exercise of powers, by:
the Register operator; or
the ACMA; or
for the purpose of obtaining legal advice in relation to this Part.
(5) For the purposes of subsection (4), this Part includes:

the disclosure is in accordance with that consent.
Authorised disclosure—information derived from protected information
(7) The ACMA may disclose personal information derived from protected information if the personal information is de-identified information (within the meaning of the Privacy Act 1988).
Offence—extended geographical jurisdiction
(8) Section 15.4 of the Criminal Code (extended geographical jurisdiction—category D) applies to an offence against subsection (1).

section.heading: Access to the National Self-exclusion Register by a licensed interactive wagering service provider

content.p: A licensed interactive wagering service provider may request the Register operator to inform the provider whether one or more specified individuals are registered individuals as at the time when the request is made.
A request under subsection (1) must include, for each individual covered by the request:
the individual’s name; and
such other information as is prescribed by the Register rules.
The Register operator must:
comply with a request under subsection (1); and
do so within the period ascertained in accordance with the Register rules.
The Register rules may make provision for and in relation to either or both of the following:
the manner in which a request under subsection (1) is to be made;
the manner in which the Register operator is to comply with a request under subsection (1).
A manner mentioned in subsection (4) must involve the use of an internet carriage service.
Connectivity obligations of licensed interactive wagering service provider
A licensed interactive wagering service provider must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the provider:
has a computer system; and
is continuously supplied with an internet carriage service;
that (when considered together) enable the provider to:
make requests under subsection (1) at any time of the day or night; and
be informed by the Register operator in compliance with those requests.
Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a licensed interactive wagering service provider; and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct contravenes subsection (6).
Penalty: 120 penalty units.
A person who contravenes subsection (7) commits a separate offence in respect of each day (including a day of conviction for the offence or any later day) during which the contravention continues.
Civil penalty provision
A licensed interactive wagering service provider must not contravene subsection (6).
Civil penalty: 180 penalty units.

A person who contravenes subsection (9) commits a separate contravention of that provision in respect of each day during which the contravention occurs (including the day the relevant civil penalty order is made or any later day).
Offence—extended geographical jurisdiction
(11) Section 15.4 of the Criminal Code (extended geographical jurisdiction—category D) applies to an offence against subsection (7).

section.heading: Access to the National Self-exclusion Register by a registered individual

content.p: A registered individual may request the Register operator to inform the individual of the content of the individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register.
The Register operator must:
comply with a request under subsection (1); and
do so as soon as practicable after the request is made.
The Register rules may make provision for and in relation to either or both of the following:
the manner in which a request under subsection (1) is to be made;
the manner in which the Register operator is to comply with a request under subsection (1).
This section does not, by implication, limit:
Australian Privacy Principle 12; or
(b) Part V of the Freedom of Information Act 1982.

section.heading: Access to the National Self-exclusion Register by a nominated support person

content.p: A nominated support person of a registered individual may request the Register operator to inform the individual of so much of the content of the individual’s entry in the National Self-exclusion Register as relates to the nominated support person.
The Register operator must:
comply with a request under subsection (1); and
do so as soon as practicable after the request is made.
The Register rules may make provision for and in relation to either or both of the following:
the manner in which a request under subsection (1) is to be made;
the manner in which the Register operator is to comply with a request under subsection (1).
This section does not, by implication, limit:
Australian Privacy Principle 12; or
(b) Part V of the Freedom of Information Act 1982.

section.heading: Disclosure to State/Territory wagering licensing or regulatory bodies

content.p: The ACMA may authorise the Register operator to disclose protected information to a State/Territory wagering licensing or regulatory body if the ACMA is satisfied that the information will enable or assist the body to perform any of the functions, or exercise any of the powers, of the body.
Conditions
The ACMA may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected information disclosed under subsection (1).
An instrument made under subsection (2) that imposes conditions relating to one particular disclosure identified in the instrument is not a legislative instrument.
Otherwise, an instrument made under subsection (2) is a legislative instrument.
An ACMA official may disclose protected information to the Minister.
An ACMA official may disclose to a Minister protected information that relates to a matter arising under a provision of an Act that is administered by that Minister.
Subsection (2) does not limit subsection (1).

section.heading: Disclosure to public servants for advising their Ministers etc.

content.p: For the purpose of advising the Minister, an ACMA official may disclose protected information to:
the Secretary of the Department; or
an APS employee in the Department who is authorised, in writing, by the Secretary of the Department for the purposes of this subsection.
For the purpose of advising a Minister administering a particular provision of an Act, an ACMA official may disclose protected information relating to a matter arising under that provision to:
the Secretary of the Department that is administered by that Minister; or
an APS employee in that Department who is authorised, in writing, by the Secretary of that Department for the purposes of this subsection.
If information is disclosed to the Secretary of the Department under subsection (1) for the purpose of advising the Minister, the Secretary may, for that purpose, disclose the information to:
the Minister; or
an APS employee in the Department who is authorised, in writing, by the Secretary of the Department for the purposes of this subsection.
If information is disclosed to an APS employee in the Department under subsection (1) for the purpose of advising the Minister, the APS employee may, for that purpose, disclose the information to:
the Minister; or
the Secretary of the Department; or
another APS employee in the Department who is authorised, in writing, by the Secretary of the Department for the purposes of this subsection.

If information is disclosed to the Secretary of a Department under subsection (2) for the purpose of advising the Minister who administers that Department, the Secretary may, for that purpose, disclose the information to:
that Minister; or
an APS employee in that Department who is authorised, in writing, by the Secretary of that Department for the purposes of this subsection.

If information is disclosed to an APS employee in a Department under subsection (2) for the purpose of advising the Minister who administers that Department, the APS employee may, for that purpose, disclose the information to:
that Minister; or
the Secretary of that Department; or
another APS employee in that Department who is authorised, in writing, by the Secretary of that Department for the purposes of this subsection.
Subsection (2) does not limit subsection (1).

section.heading: When levy is due and payable

content.p: Levy is due and payable at the time ascertained in accordance with the Register rules.
If an amount of levy payable by a person remains unpaid after the time when it became due for payment, the person is liable to pay, by way of penalty, an amount calculated at the rate of:
20% per annum; or
if the Register rules specify a lower percentage—that lower percentage per annum;
on the amount unpaid, calculated from the start of the day after that time occurred until the end of the day before the day when the amount of levy is paid in full.
(2) Penalty payable under subsection (1) is to be known as late payment penalty.
Remission of late payment penalty
The ACMA may remit the whole or a part of an amount of late payment penalty.
Review of decisions
Applications may be made to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal for review of a decision of the ACMA to refuse to remit the whole or a part of an amount under subsection (3).

section.heading: Recovery of levy and late payment penalty

content.p: Levy, or late payment penalty:
is a debt due to the ACMA on behalf of the Commonwealth; and
may be recovered by the ACMA, on behalf of the Commonwealth, in:
the Federal Court; or
the Federal Circuit Court; or
a court of a State or Territory that has jurisdiction in relation to the matter.

section.heading: Refund of overpayment of levy or late payment penalty

content.p: If there is an overpayment of:
levy; or
late payment penalty;
the overpayment is to be refunded by the ACMA on behalf of the Commonwealth.

The Register operator may arrange for the use, under the Register operator’s control, of computer programs for any purposes for which the Register operator may, or must, under this Part or the Register rules:
make a decision; or
exercise any power or comply with any obligation; or
do anything else related to making a decision or exercising a power or complying with an obligation.
For the purposes of this Part and the Register rules, the Register operator is taken to have:
made a decision; or
exercised a power or complied with an obligation; or
done something else related to the making of a decision or the exercise of a power or the compliance with an obligation;
that was made, exercised, complied with or done by the operation of a computer program under an arrangement made under subsection (1).

(3) The Register operator may substitute a decision for a decision (the initial decision) made by the operation of a computer program under an arrangement under subsection (1) if the Register operator is satisfied that the initial decision is incorrect.

The Register rules may prescribe procedures that must be followed by the Register operator in order to deal with complaints about the administration or operation of the National Self-exclusion Register.
If:
a person has reason to believe that another person has contravened a provision of:
this Part; or
the Register rules; and
the person makes a complaint to the Register operator about the matter;
the Register operator must refer the complaint to the ACMA.

section.heading: Application of the Privacy Act 1988 to the Register operator

content.p: For the purposes of the Privacy Act 1988, if the National Self-exclusion Register is kept by the Register operator under a particular contract, each of the following:
the keeping of the National Self-exclusion Register by the Register operator;
the operation of the National Self-exclusion Register by the Register operator;
the performance of a function, or the exercise of a power, by the Register operator under:
this Part; or
the Register rules;
is taken to be the provision of a service to the ACMA under the contract.

section.heading: Application of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 to the Register operator

content.p: (1) For the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 1982, if the National Self-exclusion Register is kept by the Register operator under a particular contract, the contract is taken to be a Commonwealth contract.
(2) For the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 1982, if the National Self-exclusion Register is kept by the Register operator under a particular contract, each of the following:
the keeping of the National Self-exclusion Register by the Register operator;
the operation of the National Self-exclusion Register by the Register operator;
the performance of a function, or the exercise of a power, by the Register operator under:
this Part; or
the Register rules;
is taken to be the provision of a service under the contract in connection with the performance of the functions or the exercise of the powers of the ACMA.
This Part does not apply to the extent (if any) that it would infringe any constitutional doctrine of implied freedom of political communication.
(2) Subsection (1) does not limit the application of section 15A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 to this Act.
After the end of the 12-month period beginning at the start of the proclaimed start day, the Minister must cause to be conducted a review of the operation of:
this Part (other than Divisions 4, 5 and 6); and
the remaining provisions of this Act, so far as they relate to this Part (other than Divisions 4, 5 and 6); and
the Register rules; and
(d) the National Self-exclusion Register (Cost Recovery Levy) Act 2019.
Public consultation
A review under subsection (1) must make provision for public consultation.
Report
A report of the review must:
be given to the Minister within 18 months after the end of the 12-month period mentioned in subsection (1); and
be published on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the report is given to the Minister.
The Minister must cause copies of a report under subsection (3) to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the Minister receives the report.
After the end of the 3-year period beginning at the start of the proclaimed start day, the Minister must cause to be conducted an evaluation of the operation of:
this Part; and
the remaining provisions of this Act, so far as they relate to this Part; and
the Register rules; and
the Regulatory Powers Act, so far as that Act relates to this Part; and
(e) the National Self-exclusion Register (Cost Recovery Levy) Act 2019.
Report
A report of the evaluation must:
be given to the Minister within 12 months after the end of the 3-year period mentioned in subsection (1); and
be published on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the report is given to the Minister.
(1) The ACMA may, by legislative instrument, make rules (Register rules) prescribing matters required or permitted by this Part to be prescribed by the Register rules.
The Register rules may make provision for or in relation to a matter by empowering the Register operator to make decisions of an administrative character.
Before making Register rules, the ACMA must consult the Minister.
